interface.name: fl_screencopy_manager
interface.description:
Copies the desktop, a part of it or one window into a wl_shm buffer of the client. It is meant for screenshot tools: the picture is exactly what the compositor draws (at the desktop's logical size, see wl_output.mode), but without the pointer, the Alt-Tab row, the on-screen indicator, and without the windows of the program that asks (so a screenshot tool does not photograph itself). While the screen is locked every capture fails.
A capture is a frame object: the compositor answers the capture request with buffer (what to allocate), the client makes a wl_shm buffer of that size and sends copy, and the compositor answers with ready (the pixels are in the buffer) or failed. The picture is taken when copy arrives.

request.name: capture_region
request.description: Logical pixels, from the top left of the desktop. The part outside the desktop is cut off; nothing left means failed.

request.name: capture_window

description.summary: one window, even when others cover it

request.description: id is the number fl_shell window_added gave (or window below). The picture is the window's window geometry (its title bar included, the programs draw their own), with its popups, transparent where the window is. An unknown id means failed.

request.name: list_windows

description.summary: the windows in view, topmost first

request.description: Answered by one window event for every window that is on the screen right now (on the workspace in view, not minimized, not one of the asking program's), then windows_done. For a "click a window" picker.

entry.name: invalid_buffer
entry.summary: the buffer does not fit what buffer announced

request.name: copy

description.summary: take the picture into this buffer

request.description: The buffer must be a wl_shm buffer of the size and stride from the buffer event and in the format from it or the other 32 bit one (argb8888 and xrgb8888 are accepted for every capture; xrgb8888 gets alpha 255). One copy per frame.

event.name: buffer

description.summary: what to allocate; sent right after the capture request

event.description: format is a wl_shm format: xrgb8888 for the desktop and regions, argb8888 for windows.

event.name: ready
event.summary: the pixels are in the buffer

event.name: failed
event.summary: no picture (locked, window gone, nothing to capture); the frame is dead
